statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-33634 is a supply-chain compromise of upstream Trivy release artifacts, including the malicious v0.69.4 release binary and v0.69.5/v0.69.6 Docker Hub images, injected at build or publish time via stolen Aqua credentials in March 2026. The malicious code was not committed to the Trivy source tree. The Trivy Operator image builds v0.31.1 from source and embeds github.com/aquasecurity/trivy v0.71.0 as a Go module dependency, which was published after the incident from clean source; the compromised release artifact code is not present in the runtime binary.

CVE-2026-33634 is a supply-chain compromise of trivy release binaries v0.69.4 through v0.69.6, injected at build time via stolen Aqua credentials in March 2026. The malicious code was never committed to the trivy source tree. zot v2.1.17 depends on github.com/aquasecurity/trivy v0.70.0, which Aqua's post-incident disclosure confirms was rebuilt from clean main; the vulnerable code is not present in this version. The product PURL pins trivy v0.70.0; re-evaluate this statement if zot's go.mod moves trivy to a different version.

CVE-2026-33634 is a supply chain compromise that affected only the upstream aquasecurity/trivy v0.69.4 release published on 2026-03-19. The CVE description explicitly identifies versions 0.69.2 and 0.69.3 of the Trivy binary as known-safe. The DHI alpine variant ships trivy 0.70.0 or later (currently 0.71.0), which was tagged and built from the rebuilt upstream source after the incident with rotated credentials and is not the malicious v0.69.4 artifact. The DHI debian variants build trivy 0.69.3 from source with COMMIT_SHA verification (commit 6fb20c8edd70745d6b34bff0387b53b03c8a760a) and never pull the upstream prebuilt binary; this scanner false positive does not affect them. The advisory range >=0.69.4 with no fixed version is overly broad relative to the actual incident scope. Every DHI trivy build is produced from clean upstream source (the git tag for debian, the rebuilt apk for alpine) and never the compromised registry artifacts, at any version, so the trivy product is matched version-lessly here to keep this statement valid across version bumps; the earlier per-version PURLs are retained for older builds.
